questions.question: Which way of running a Spring Boot app suits a production server that has Java but not Maven or the source code?
options: Packaging a JAR and running java -jar
Running javac on the main class
questions.explanation: The packaged JAR contains your classes and every library, so the server only needs Java.

questions.question: application.properties has server.port=8081, and the app starts with: SERVER_PORT=8082 java -Dserver.port=8083 -jar app.jar --server.port=8084. Which port does it use?
questions.explanation: Command-line arguments beat JVM options, which beat environment variables, which beat application.properties.

questions.question: A developer edits a controller, then runs java -jar target/app.jar again, but the response has not changed. What is the most likely cause?
options: The JAR was not rebuilt with ./mvnw package after the change
The browser cache stores every Spring Boot response
Spring Boot needs a restart twice to load new code
questions.explanation: java -jar runs the JAR as it was last packaged, so code changes need a new ./mvnw package first.

questions.question: ./mvnw spring-boot:run --server.port=9091 fails with "Unrecognized option: --server.port=9091". How should the port be passed?
options: It cannot be changed when using Maven
questions.explanation: Maven reads options itself, so app arguments go through the spring-boot.run.arguments property.

questions.question: A @Component implements CommandLineRunner and prints "BusGo is ready". Where does that line appear in the startup log?
options: Only when the first request arrives
questions.explanation: Runners are called once the app has fully started, so their output follows the Started message.
